newsitem.title: GERMANY: Computer 2000 says U.S. unit dims outlook.
newsitem.headline: Computer 2000 says U.S. unit dims outlook.

text.p: German computer distributor Computer 2000 AG said Thursday that losses at its U.S. unit Ameriquest dampened its earnings outlook despite a 33 percent rise in first-quarter sales to 2.1 billion marks ($1.2 billion).

The company, 75 percent owned by diversified German utility Viag AG, said first-quarter earnings in Europe and the Middle East were above target, but Ameriquest Technologies Inc. was still losing money.
Although a turnaround at Ameriquest had not met expectations, Chief Executive Walter von Szcytnicki said the company expected group sales to grow by more than 50 percent over the next three years.

In the year ended Sept. 30, Computer 2000 registered a pre-tax profit of 10 million marks ($6 million), but suffered a net loss of 15.6 million marks ($9.23 million) due to a loss of 52 million marks ($30.8 million) at Ameriquest.
Ameriquest's stock was unchanged at 68.75 cents in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
